channel.title: Diffbrief · Security
channel.description: Daily security stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: Skimming scripts found on five retailer sites could capture payment details before checkout
item.description: Scripts were planted on five retailers' sites, and one observed instance sent test-card details to a third party before checkout validation; the scripts were removed, but any real data theft is unknown. The incident highlights exposure in client-side payment flows.

item.title: Soundness bugs can let proof checkers accept false statements
item.description: The page catalogs reported soundness bugs in proof-checking programs and advises minimizing the trusted computing base. Engineers building verification tools should consider how bugs in the checker can undermine every proof it accepts.

item.title: Attackers exploit a second Drupal flaw that can enable site takeover
item.description: Drupal says a newly patched flaw leaves some sites in unusual or incomplete install states vulnerable to takeover, and attackers are exploiting it. Operators should review the advisory and patch affected Drupal deployments.

item.title: Passkeys leave recovery dependent on providers and device syncing
item.description: The author distinguishes syncing passkeys among a provider’s devices from restoring access after losing those devices or an account. That recovery trade-off matters when engineers design authentication and account-recovery flows.

item.title: SAP investigates reported breach of its software development environment
item.description: SAP confirmed suspicious activity after reports that attackers used employee authentication tokens to access source code in its GitHub environment; the company said it had found no evidence of customer-data access. The incident highlights the downstream risk of compromised developer credentials.

item.title: Unpatched Cacti flaw reportedly allows unauthenticated remote command execution
item.description: A publicly disclosed Cacti zero-day is reported to allow unauthenticated command execution, and a proof of concept has been published. Since monitoring servers may hold credentials for other systems, operators should follow Cacti security advisories and assess exposure.

item.title: SAP confirms security incident after suspicious GitHub activity
item.description: SAP says it acted on suspicious activity, while reports allege attackers used stolen employee tokens to copy and modify source code; SAP reports no evidence of downstream customer compromise. The incident makes developer-token security a concern beyond an organization’s own codebase.

item.title: Bluetooth pairing flaw reportedly exposes affected hosts to root access
item.description: The report describes a flaw that can expose a shell on affected Bluetooth stacks after pairing, with a separate issue leading to root access. Engineers responsible for endpoint security should check vendor advisories for affected systems.

item.title: Linux NFS heap overflow enables remote root access on exposed servers
item.description: A 12-year-old heap buffer overflow in nfsd can give unauthenticated attackers root access when NFSv4.1 or 4.2 is running and TCP port 2049 is reachable. Operators need to check exposure and kernel versions.

item.title: Attackers chain PHP flaws and Fragnesia to gain root on PAN-OS devices
item.description: Attacks combine unauthenticated PHP code execution with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw on devices with internet-exposed management interfaces. The confirmed chain makes exposure and patch status of network appliances an urgent operational concern.

item.title: Socket offers free patches for patchable critical RubyGems CVEs
item.description: Socket says it has patches for all patchable critical-severity RubyGems CVEs and makes them available without requiring dependency upgrades. This approach could help teams secure applications where upgrades are risky or impractical.

item.title: Fake expert interviews target corporate Google and Okta credentials
item.description: A campaign impersonates eight brands with paid interview and webinar invitations, using legitimate email and event platforms to distribute credential-stealing links. The abuse of trusted services is a useful reminder to account for them in phishing defenses.

item.title: Compromised employee GitHub account lets attacker inject code at 1Password
item.description: An attacker used an employee account to access private repositories, modify backend services and steal customer records, though vaults and their encryption keys were not compromised. The incident puts CI/CD access and deployment controls in focus.

item.title: Most exploited flaws in a vendor advisory report came from bundled software
item.description: Of 38 advisories covering vulnerabilities in CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, 33 involved bundled components such as PHP, Node.js and OpenSSH. Exposure can persist until appliance vendors rebuild products with upstream fixes.

item.title: Remus steals Gmail messages through a malicious Chrome extension
item.description: Researchers found that Remus’s advertised Gmail “zero-day” is a Chrome extension that steals unread mail and remains effective after password changes or session revocations. The case shows why browser extensions can outlast account-level recovery steps.

item.title: SYS010 uses browser management to install an email-stealing extension
item.description: The malware arrives through ads for animated wallpapers and enrolls browsers in enterprise-style management to force an extension that can read or delete Gmail and Outlook messages. It illustrates how browser management features can be abused to persistently control endpoints.

item.title: Leaked Gemini API keys can turn a prototype into a large unexpected bill
item.description: The guide describes developer keys scattered across environment files, shell profiles, chat threads and app configs, and warns that exposed credentials can drive large workloads and bills. Teams moving AI prototypes into production need a deliberate path off raw keys.

item.title: Defang attacker used an overprivileged GitHub App to reach deployment credentials
item.description: An attacker accessed Defang’s build system, copied deployment credentials, and downloaded its main database; a testing GitHub App had excess permissions, including changing deployment environments. The incident offers concrete lessons on CI/CD credential scope and checks affected users should perform.

item.title: A pre-auth Linux NFS server flaw can give remote attackers root access
item.description: A heap overflow in Linux nfsd lets one unauthenticated connection to reachable TCP 2049 write past a kernel object and chain to root; the advisory says to patch or firewall the port. NFS operators should prioritize checking exposure and rebooting onto a fixed kernel.

item.title: 1Password says attacker used employee GitHub account to push malicious code
item.description: The attacker accessed source code and pushed code that downloaded customer names, email addresses and account metadata; 1Password says vault contents were not accessed. It offers a concrete account of a supply-chain incident affecting a widely used security service.

item.title: GreyNoise tracks an active intrusion campaign against Check Point management servers
item.description: GreyNoise describes tracking an active intrusion campaign against Check Point security management servers using its sensor network. Operators of those systems should consult the full report for the campaign details and any response guidance.

item.title: Dangling DNS records enabled low-cost AWS IP takeovers on Treasury domains
item.description: Researchers demonstrated that attackers could claim AWS Elastic IPs targeted by dangling DNS records, finding real takeovers on US Treasury domains that were reported and fixed. The finding makes auditing stale DNS records an urgent cloud-security task.

item.title: iTerm2 Kitty image handling enabled command execution through injected responses
item.description: A crafted file path could make an error response write newline-separated commands to the terminal’s stdin; affected versions are 3.6.1–3.7.8, fixed in 3.7.9. The flaw worked on default installations, making the parser and terminal-response boundary worth reviewing.

item.title: Hex.pm blocked a server-command exploit but cannot rule out database access
item.description: An attacker exploited a flaw to run commands on Hex.pm servers; the fix was deployed within 20 minutes, with no evidence of package or database changes. Database reads were not logged, so stored credentials and account data may have been exposed.

item.title: CHERIoT research extends formal verification toward bug-finding
item.description: The Cerise project developed proofs in Rocq using Iris, broadened the properties studied, and moved toward an instruction set closer to CHERIoT. It shows how formal methods can be extended to reason about security properties in capability systems.

item.title: Rust Foundation scanner uses decision models to flag suspicious crates
item.description: A scanner has run on the crate firehose for a little over a week, using decision models to flag potentially malicious packages for human review. The early operational account may help engineers assess automated supply-chain screening.

item.title: NGINX HTTP/2 use-after-free can cause denial of service under connection pressure
item.description: A fragmented request can leave an active connection marked reusable; under pressure, NGINX may free memory still used by that request, causing denial of service, with code execution described as possible under specific conditions. Operators of HTTP/2 proxy servers should review exposure and the relevant advisories.

item.title: Android researcher reports 95 findings and a $250 total bounty
item.description: The researcher says 95 reports went to Google’s Android and Devices vulnerability programs, about 95% with functional proof of concept, for a total payout of $250. The account raises practical questions about vulnerability reporting incentives in a widely deployed platform.

item.title: upki shares browser-grade certificate signals across TLS clients
item.description: upki provides a compact, automatically updated local cache of revocation, distrust-date, and Certificate Transparency signals for TLS stacks. The proposal addresses how non-browser clients can narrow trust after an incident without waiting for platform trust-store updates.

item.title: Multiple security products can deadlock through crossed detours
item.description: Two anti-malware products can deadlock when their hooks create a reversed lock hierarchy—for example, one detour reaches the network while another reaches the registry. Engineers integrating low-level system software should account for interactions beyond simple product exclusions.

item.title: A new HTML element enables XSS in innerHTML without an equals sign
item.description: A researcher found a way to solve an injection challenge previously considered impossible by using a newly introduced HTML element. The result highlights how parser behavior can undermine assumptions in web input handling.

item.title: Shirudo shields running Linux services while operators roll out patches
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco describe a runtime shield that can protect Linux systems during patch rollout; a controlled test blocked a Java4Shell attempt against Elasticsearch without a restart. Operators can evaluate it as a way to reduce exposure while patching.

item.title: Project Zero finds three new VirtualBox process-protection bypasses
item.description: A 2026 review found three new ways around VirtualBox's Windows protected-process mechanism and a broken fix for an earlier bypass. The findings are relevant to engineers evaluating the security boundaries of desktop virtualization.

item.title: Thirteen NuGet packages used fake job assessments to deliver malware
item.description: Socket found packages posing as .NET UI controls that could download payloads, stage DLL side-loading, or run an executable; one package remained listed at publication. .NET teams should scrutinize dependencies introduced through assessment projects and check whether affected packages were used.

item.title: Dependency maintenance leaves software packagers with a growing security burden
item.description: The author argues that complex dependency trees leave downstream maintainers carrying risk when upstream components become unreliable, and questions whether software is getting less secure. The perspective highlights the human and operational limits of patching dependencies.

item.title: A personal security checklist argues against keeping SSH keys on disk
item.description: The author describes pruning unused services, putting most services behind Tailscale and keeping servers updated before turning to personal-device security. The advice is a reminder to reduce exposure across both hosted systems and developer machines.

item.title: Targeted MP4 fuzzers address gaps in GStreamer demuxer testing
item.description: The post examines why conventional mutation-based fuzzing struggles with MP4 and describes targeted fuzzers built for GStreamer's qtdemux element, which uncovered vulnerabilities. The techniques may help teams testing complex media parsers and other structured formats.

item.title: Alpine volunteers responded to PHP2Shell and a GitLab RCE disruption
item.description: The excerpt says PHP2Shell and a GitLab RCE disrupted Alpine services while volunteers worked to revive the wiki and publish an incident announcement. It gives a glimpse of the response burden on community-run infrastructure, though few technical details are included.

item.title: GL.iNet fixes exploited cloud flaw that infected routers and KVM devices
item.description: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet’s cloud remote-management service to install malware on some routers and KVM devices; the vendor says to install the security firmware to remove it. The incident highlights that fixing a cloud entry point alone does not clean already infected devices.

item.title: PSF applies organization-wide policies to block risky GitHub Actions triggers
item.description: The Python Software Foundation removed dangerous triggers from its GitHub organizations and explains how to roll out policies that block them; some triggers can expose secrets to workflows started by strangers. The guidance covers checking what a policy would block before enforcing it.

item.title: Upload2Shell chains anonymous IPP printing into command execution on Debian
item.description: A remote print job through a shared CUPS queue on Debian 13 reportedly ran a command as the lp user; the chain involves Ghostscript 10.05.1. Engineers running exposed print services should assess their risk, though the excerpt gives no remediation steps.

item.title: PHP updates fix seven critical flaws that can enable unauthenticated RCE
item.description: PHP updates address 17 vulnerabilities across supported branches, including seven rated critical; one flaw involves malformed, partially written session files. Exposed PHP deployments need the updates because earlier PHP2Shell mitigations do not cover these vectors.

item.title: GitHub Actions security controls must account for valid stolen credentials
item.description: The guide focuses on attackers using legitimate maintainer credentials or tokens, which can make malicious requests indistinguishable from normal work. It covers GitHub Actions, trusted publishing, release approvals and credential revocation for teams hardening CI/CD.

item.title: OPTIMJACK injected malicious JavaScript into at least 178 organizations’ sites
item.description: Attackers exploited Optimizely Web Experimentation to serve malicious JavaScript from the vendor’s CDN to visitors of at least 178 organizations. The incident shows how a trusted third-party script can become production code and bypass defenses focused on a site’s own infrastructure.

item.title: Optimizely compromise spread malicious scripts across 178 organizations
item.description: The attack injected JavaScript through Optimizely snippets used by 178 organizations, with payloads for cryptocurrency theft, payment-card theft and iOS malware. Teams relying on third-party experimentation scripts should treat those scripts as part of their production attack surface.

item.title: GPGME double-free flaw can expose data from crafted OpenPGP user IDs
item.description: A crafted, very long OpenPGP user ID triggers a double free that can be used to exfiltrate application data; remote code execution cannot be ruled out. GPGME 2.3.1 fixes the flaw, making the advisory actionable for affected software.

item.title: Ghostscript font-loader bugs and a -dSAFER bypass enable file-triggered RCE
item.description: The research describes memory corruption in Ghostscript's font loader and a -dSAFER sandbox bypass that can lead to remote command execution through file-processing paths. Engineers should check whether their applications invoke Ghostscript on untrusted files.

item.title: Ruby's ruby2shell is a heap overflow; Cloudflare adds WAF rules
item.description: Ruby's critical string-case heap overflow can enable unauthenticated RCE in default Rails and classic Sinatra configurations; fixes are available in Ruby 3.3.14, 3.4.13, and 4.0.10. Cloudflare's WAF is only a compensating control, so affected deployments still need patching.

item.title: phpAfterShell can enable RCE through PHP's default file-session handler
item.description: The PHP session-handler flaw can lead to RCE, and fixed releases are available across PHP 8.2–8.6; Cloudflare updated its WAF rule to block known patterns. The WAF details help with immediate mitigation, but affected PHP installations need the security updates.

item.title: Reported NGINX flaws may enable unauthenticated RCE and container-host takeover
item.description: The report describes an unauthenticated command-execution flaw when HTTP/2 is enabled and a kernel SCTP privilege-escalation flaw that could let an attacker escape a container to the host. It recommends updating to NGINX 1.31.9, making the claims important for operators to assess.

item.title: UK teams secure tens of thousands of refrigeration units after a flaw is found
item.description: Researchers and the NCSC worked with companies to secure refrigeration units after finding a flaw that could have enabled worse damage. It is a useful reminder that operational technology in widely deployed supply chains needs coordinated security response.

item.title: Election sites faced 180 times more vulnerability attempts than DDoS attacks
item.description: Cloudflare reports that U.S. government election sites saw vulnerability attempts at 180 times the rate of DDoS attacks, with daily exploit attempts rising from 200,000 in January to 2 million in October. The shift toward access to internal systems and data offers useful context for prioritizing defenses.

item.title: Ruby2ßhell enables pre-authentication RCE in stock Rails configurations
item.description: The flaw affects Rails and Sinatra in their default configurations across multiple Ruby versions; the excerpt lists patched releases for several bundled products. Teams should check their Ruby and framework versions and apply available fixes.

item.title: OpenSSL EVP_EncodeBlock buffer overflow stems from invalid inputs
item.description: The proposed fix rejects null buffers, negative lengths, and encoded sizes that overflow an int; the excerpt says a large `-proxy_pass` can trigger the issue through `openssl s_client`. Engineers using OpenSSL should track the fix and assess exposure to this input path.

item.title: Five nginx memory-corruption flaws enable crashes or command execution
item.description: Five unauthenticated nginx flaws can crash workers or run commands; a separate Linux kernel bug can escalate a foothold to host root, including from a Docker container. nginx operators should patch, while Cloudflare proxying blocks some of the most serious paths but is not a substitute for updates.

item.title: Java4Shell enables remote code execution through OpenJDK’s Base64 decoder
item.description: Malformed Base64 input can corrupt memory in OpenJDK, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution against several products in default configurations. OpenJDK and Oracle released patches, and Cloudflare added WAF rules; teams should update affected runtimes rather than rely on filtering alone.

item.title: OpenJDK AVX-512 Base64 path can write past output on invalid input
item.description: The reported bug in the x86-64 AVX-512 decoder can write past the logical output length when invalid Base64 input leaves fewer than four bytes; the suggested fix is to return to Java early. Engineers maintaining affected OpenJDK code should assess the path and proposed fix.

item.title: Synology patches critical flaw enabling arbitrary file access
item.description: A critical flaw in Synology DSM and BeeStation OS can let remote attackers read or write arbitrary files or cause denial of service; the advisory recommends upgrades or disabling the OAuth Service package. Operators should check affected versions and mitigations for their deployments.

item.title: Java4Shell affects a JVM Base64 intrinsic; disable it while upgrading
item.description: The issue stems from handwritten assembly used for Base64 intrinsics in the Java Virtual Machine; the excerpt recommends `-XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics` until upgrading to a patched VM. Java operators need to know the mitigation, though the excerpt omits affected versions and impact details.

item.title: PHP 8.2–8.5 security releases fix critical remote-code-execution flaws
item.description: Four PHP maintenance releases address critical vulnerabilities that could allow remote code execution; the cited announcement says they require non-default configurations or uncommon setups. PHP deployments should check the affected release notes and apply vendor updates.

item.title: ARMORY CASTLE exploited an unauthenticated vCenter session-key disclosure flaw
item.description: The report says ARMORY CASTLE exploited CVE-2026-123890 in VMware vCenter Server, an unauthenticated SRP-6a session-key disclosure vulnerability. vCenter operators should consult the advisory for affected versions and remediation details; the excerpt does not provide them.

item.title: Two critical NGINX flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution
item.description: Two critical flaws can let attackers take over affected NGINX servers; both require HTTP/2 to be enabled, and one affects versions dating back to 1.9.5. NGINX’s role at the front of many production systems makes assessing exposure important.

item.title: Seven Ruby flaws include heap overflow and double free with RCE potential
item.description: Ruby's advisory describes seven flaws in regular expressions and string case conversion, including bugs with proof-of-concept remote-code-execution scenarios, and recommends upgrading to Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13, or 3.3.14. Teams running Ruby should assess exposure and apply the patched releases.

item.title: Researchers report five nginx RCE flaws and a Linux kernel privilege escalation
item.description: The report says five nginx flaws each allow unauthenticated remote code execution under different configurations, alongside a Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw. It includes exposure checks and mitigation steps for operators.

item.title: Optimizely vulnerability exposed visitors to malware on at least 178 major sites
item.description: A vulnerability involving Optimizely led to malware being served on at least 178 destinations, including the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger, and Zoom. The incident underscores the risks of third-party scripts on widely visited sites.

item.title: PyPI tightens checks on uploaded package distributions
item.description: PyPI is adding stricter validation for source distributions and wheels to reduce parser differentials, with further conformance checks planned. Package maintainers may need current Python versions and build backends that produce compliant archives.

item.title: COLD RELIC turns stolen identities and cloud data into further compromises
item.description: Mandiant describes linked intrusions in which COLD RELIC used data, a corporate staff directory and identities stolen in an earlier compromise to target another organization. The account highlights how a cloud compromise can create risks beyond the initially breached company.

item.title: Emittr turns a rooted Android phone into a USB HID keyboard for locked-down hosts
item.description: Emittr uses Android's USB gadget subsystem to present a rooted phone as a keyboard and mouse, requiring no software on the target host. The technique is useful to understand for both air-gapped workflows and the limits of host-side controls.

item.title: Java pre-auth RCE affects versions 17, 21, 25 and 27 before patched builds
item.description: The reported unauthenticated RCE affects Java 17, 21, 25 and 27 releases before specified patched builds; Java 8 and 11 are listed as unaffected. Operators should check their Java lines and apply the corresponding updates.

item.title: OpenJDK Base64 decoder bug can corrupt memory on x86-64
item.description: The reported flaw is in OpenJDK’s optimized x86-64 Base64 decoder, where malformed input can overwrite neighboring memory and potentially expose data or enable remote code execution. Runtime maintainers should assess exposure and follow vendor advisories.

item.title: Optimizely signup-flow flaw let attackers inject malware into major websites
item.description: Attackers exploited Optimizely’s Experimentation signup flow to add malicious JavaScript to customer projects, affecting sites including Zoom, CNN, BBC, Salesforce, and GitLab. The company says it blocked the vulnerable path; teams using the platform should check their exposure.

item.title: Researchers examine brute-forcing Windows Hello PINs through TPM counter rollback
item.description: The paper examines how firmware TPM lockout state stored in SPI flash relies on JEDEC Replay Protected Monotonic Counters for rollback prevention, and targets brute-forcing Windows Hello PINs. Engineers should assess the hardware trust boundary behind PIN rate limits on deployed Windows devices.

item.title: Phrack 73 includes container escapes, kernel exploits and AI security
item.description: The issue’s contents include work on escaping Docker through vDSO, kernel exploits, AI-related security and Chromium sandbox escapes. Security engineers can use the table of contents to find relevant research, though the listing provides no article details.

item.title: Phrack 73 covers Docker escapes, browser sandboxes and AI-era exploits
item.description: The issue’s table of contents includes work on escaping Docker through vDSO, Chromium renderer sandbox escapes, WinFsp zero-days and kernel exploitation in the LLM era. Those topics offer security engineers several areas to investigate, though the listing provides little detail on the pieces.

item.title: Compromised Optimizely JavaScript served malware to visitors at 178 organizations
item.description: Malicious scripts delivered credential and payment theft, crypto-wallet swapping, and iOS exploit kits through Optimizely; the excerpt says CSP enforcement could have blocked key parts. Teams relying on third-party JavaScript should examine their supply-chain controls.

item.title: Injected Optimizely scripts skim cards and replace crypto addresses on major sites
item.description: Malicious JavaScript in Optimizely bundles reportedly skims card forms, swaps pasted crypto addresses, and exfiltrates page data from visitors to named sites. Teams using Optimizely should inspect their bundles and assess visitor exposure.

item.title: macOS 27.3 lets users limit apps to selected protected folders
item.description: Starting in macOS 27.3, users can grant access to specific protected folders or apps instead of Full Disk Access or System & App Protection Override. Granular permissions are a useful security design pattern for desktop software.

item.title: NoisyTCP reports pre-authentication remote corruption in the Linux kernel
item.description: A post on oss-security identifies CVE-2026-99288 as a pre-authentication remote corruption flaw in Linux kernel TCP, but the excerpt gives no affected versions or mitigation. Kernel operators need the full advisory to assess exposure and response.

item.title: uBlock Origin’s element picker let websites inject trusted filters and run JavaScript
item.description: A website could trick uBlock Origin into adding a trusted filter, then use it to run JavaScript on other sites; the issue is fixed. The case exposes a risky trust boundary in browser extensions and describes AI-assisted vulnerability discovery.

item.title: Fireworks AI breach exposed Uber drivers' data through stolen vendor credentials
item.description: Hackers used credentials stolen from Fireworks AI to access Uber data, including drivers’ personal and license information; the breach also affected Notion data. It shows how a breach at an AI vendor can expose data held by downstream customers.

item.title: Attackers repurposed old inactive Bitly links to redirect visitors
item.description: Bitly said bad actors could repurpose certain old, inactive links and redirect visitors to unrelated content; it suspended accounts and disabled affected links. The incident highlights the risks of relying on long-lived short URLs.

item.title: Webloc ad surveillance has reached security agencies in multiple countries
item.description: Citizen Lab used open-source research, records requests and infrastructure mapping to identify Webloc customers, with Bloomberg finding additional agencies across several countries. The investigation shows how advertising data systems can be repurposed for state surveillance.

item.title: A NetBSD guide separates disk-loss secrecy from tamper resistance
item.description: The guide distinguishes protection for a lost or stolen device from protection against tampering, and focuses on the first threat model. Clear threat-model boundaries help engineers choose what disk encryption must protect.

item.title: Railway’s hack postmortem examines attackers’ likely use of unguarded AI models
item.description: Railway’s postmortem reportedly details a hack in which the attacker likely used AI models without safeguards, and the platform hardened its systems afterward. The incident offers security lessons for engineers operating cloud platforms, though this summary provides few specifics.

item.title: Datasette 0.65.6 fixes unauthorized database-file downloads
item.description: A database registered under a different route from its name could be downloaded by actors denied access to it; version 0.65.6 backports the fix. Teams exposing Datasette databases should check their versions and route permissions.

item.title: Lovable-built apps exposed passport details and over 200,000 private messages
item.description: Researchers examined 159,041 Lovable projects and found personal and confidential data accessible without login, including passport details and more than 200,000 private messages. Teams using AI app builders should independently verify access controls before handling sensitive data.

item.title: PyPI redesign makes package security signals clearer
item.description: PyPI's redesigned project pages surface security signals and package details, including provenance attestations whose meaning and limits were previously hard to understand. Clearer signals can help engineers assess supply-chain risk when choosing dependencies.

item.title: Google Project Zero drops the extra 30-day disclosure window
item.description: Project Zero is moving from a 90-day deadline plus 30 days of rollout time to a 90-day policy, citing AI-assisted discovery and exploitation that raise immediate risk. Security teams should account for faster-moving disclosure and remediation timelines.

item.title: FBI says North Korean hackers used fake video calls in a $400M crypto theft
item.description: The FBI says the campaign used fake video calls to steal victims' identities, with more than 900 victims and over $400M in cryptocurrency taken in 18 months. The account illustrates the scale and social-engineering tactics of a major cybercrime campaign.

item.title: Apify incident response adds hashed API tokens and internal network restrictions
item.description: Apify says it now stores API tokens only as hashes, added internal network restrictions and stronger authentication, and recommends users restrict storage access. The root cause is still under investigation, so the full incident lessons are pending.

item.title: A Burp skill finds CSP bypasses in allowed script sources
item.description: The skill checks allowed script sources for known bypass gadgets and examines form-action policy, then can build a proof of concept that exfiltrates to Burp Collaborator. It automates a tedious part of CSP review for security engineers.

item.title: Falcon C2 uses malicious browser JavaScript to steal credentials and session data
item.description: The framework runs malicious JavaScript in compromised webmail and government sites, and has been used to sideload Chrome extensions and steal passwords, emails, and session cookies. The browser-based technique is relevant to teams securing web applications and user sessions.
